{{Short description|German manager and politician}}
[[File:Plenarrede Dr. Thomas Gambke (2013).jpg|thumb|Gambke holding a speech in 2013]]
'''Thomas Gambke''' is a retired German politician of the [[Alliance 90/The Greens]], who was a member of the [[Bundestag]] from 2005 to 2017, effectively winning a seat in the [[2005 German federal election|15th]], [[2009 German federal election|16th]] and [[2013 German federal election|17th]] election. A diploma physician, Gambke worked for the [[Schott AG]] and later as an independent entrepreneur, prior to entering politics.

== Early life and career ==
Gambke was born on October 16, 1949 in [[Rimsting]], at the [[Lake Chiemsee]] in Upper [[Bavaria]]. He visited a ''[[Volksschule]]'' in Mehlem (Bonn) and went to [[Gymnasium (Germany)|''Gymnasium'']] in [[Bad Godesberg]] (Bonn) and [[Gehrden]]. After graduating in 1968 and completing Basic military service, Gambke studied [[physics]] at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]] where he got his diploma in 1976, followed by a [[doctorate]] in 1981.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Deutscher Bundestag - Dr. Thomas Gambke, Bündnis 90/Die Grünen |url=https://www.bundestag.de/webarchiv/abgeordnete/biografien18/G/gambke_thomas-258416 |access-date=2024-09-20 |website=Deutscher Bundestag |language=de}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Lebenslauf |url=http://www.t-gambke.de/persoenliches/lebenslauf.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170719202408/http://www.t-gambke.de/persoenliches/lebenslauf.html |archive-date=19 Jul 2017 |access-date=20 Sep 2024 |website=t-gambke.de}}</ref>

He worked as a research assistant at the Institut für Festkörperphysik (Institute for [[Solid-state physics|Solid State Physics]]) at the Technische Universität Darmstadt and did scientific work at the [[University of California, San Diego]], From 1982, he was as a technology consultant at the {{Ill|VDI Technology Center|de|VDI Technologiezentrum}} in Berlin.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

Gambke joined [[Schott AG]] in 1984 where he first worked as a project manager in the Research & Development department. He became that department's head in 1985 and did research at the [[Otto Schott Research Center]] in Mainz. In 1990, Gambke took over the commercial management of the Schott plant in [[Landshut]]. He contributed to the creation of production facilities in Czechia (1992), Singapore (1994) and in the USA (2001).<ref name=":0" />

Towards the end of his time at Schott, he held high positions in Schott: He was the head of Schott's Packaging Department and the vice-president of the newly founded ''NEC SCHOTT Components Corporation''. Last he was the Spokesman of the Executive Board of ''SCHOTT Electronics GmbH'' from 2003 to 2006.<ref name=":0" />

Gambke left Schott in 2007 and founded ''Bürgerenergie Isae e.G.'' in 2012, an organization focussing on [[Energy transition]]. He was a member of the board of trustees of the [[University of Applied Sciences Landshut]] and a member of the [[Petra Kelly]] Foundation, named after one of the founders of the Green Party.<ref name=":0" />

== Political Work ==
Gambke joined the [[Alliance 90/The Greens]] in 2004 and was the spokesman of the party's local chapter in the [[Landshut (district)|Landshut District]] from 2006 to 2010. He was a member of the city Council of Landshut from 2008 to 2011. During that time, he was first elected into the Bundestag (in 2009). There, he was a member of the Finance Committee, the Committee for Economy and Energy and was the chairman of the Parliamentary group organizing cooperation with [[ASEAN]] countries.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ämter und Funktionen |url=http://www.t-gambke.de/persoenliches/aemter-und-funktionen.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170719201654/http://www.t-gambke.de/persoenliches/aemter-und-funktionen.html |archive-date=19 Jul 2017 |access-date=21 Sep 2024 |website=t-gambke.de}}</ref>

== Private Life ==
Gambke is married and has three children. He lives in Landshut.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> According to himself, his biggest political idol is [[Ernst Reuter]] of the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]], the first mayor of Berlin after WWII.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Über mich |url=http://www.t-gambke.de/persoenliches/ueber-mich.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170621055059/http://www.t-gambke.de/persoenliches/ueber-mich.html |archive-date=21 Jun 2017 |access-date=21 Sep 2024 |website=t-gambke.de}}</ref>
